changes.text: 原计划要宏大得多：若能按时登陆，横穿队伍就立刻出发，踏上1800英里的行程，希望在五个月内穿越极点，抵达罗斯海一侧的基地；若登陆太晚，就先越冬，在秋季和次年春季布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。船被压毁之后，任务换成了另一件事——让全队上岸。

The plan he began with was far grander. If the landing was made in time, "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Should the landing be made too late in the season, the party would go into winter quarters, lay out depots during the autumn and the following spring, and set out as early as possible in 1915. Once the ice had crushed the ship, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.
后来他们真的做了第二次尝试：行军七天，直线只前进了七英里半；照这个速度，要三百多天才能到西边的陆地，而食物只够四十二天，只好再次在浮冰上扎营。新的营地叫耐心营，他们在那里住了将近三个半月。

Later they did make that second attempt. They marched for seven days and gained seven and a half miles in a direct line; at that rate it would take over three hundred days to reach the land to the west, and they had food for only forty-two days. So they camped once more on the floe. They called the new camp Patience Camp and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定都在衡量眼前的路还能不能走下去。扎营等待也不是新想法：行军开始前，他就写下过在最近的厚浮冰上扎营、等浮冰外漂到开阔水面的方案，但他确信应当先尝试行军，还特别提到这个问题有心理层面的考虑——让大家觉得自己正在朝陆地走，比坐等漂流要好。海洋营是在四天苦干之后回到这个先前否决过的方案：营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望——附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地——等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。

One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared and a good floe turned up, they moved on after lunch. Both decisions turned on whether the way ahead could be made. Nor was camping to wait a new idea. Before the march began he had already written down the option of camping on the nearest heavy floe and awaiting the outward drift of the pack to open water, but he felt sure it was right to attempt a march first, noting that there was a psychological aspect too: the men would be better off feeling they were on their way to land than simply sitting and waiting for the drift. Ocean Camp, after four days of hard effort, was a return to that option he had set aside. The camp went onto a more solid floe, the reasoning carried a specific hope (leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west), and a second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.

另一种解释是关于取舍的标准（作者推断）：金币被扔掉、照片被留下，他其实写了理由。他说自己对每人两磅的限额本就有些舍不得，因为极想把重量压到最低，但有些个人物品确实可以算作不可或缺：旅程可能很长，到另一头还可能要在荒凉的海岸上临时越冬，人在这种处境下需要有东西占住思绪，需要一件能想起远在海外的家乡和亲人的实物。扉页则被他撕了下来，这段记述没有写它的去向。作者的理解是：那道上限筛的不只是重量；在冰上，金币换不来什么，照片却能让人想起家。

A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. The sovereigns were thrown away and the photographs were kept, and he did give his reasons. He admits he rather grudged the two-pound allowance per man, so anxious was he to keep weights down, but some personal belongings could fairly be regarded as indispensable: the journey might be a long one, and there might be a winter in improvised quarters on an inhospitable coast at the other end. In his words, "A man under such conditions needs something to occupy his thoughts, some tangible memento of his home and people beyond the seas." The fly-leaf was torn out, and the passage does not say what became of it. The author's understanding is that the limit screened for more than weight: on the ice the gold coins could buy nothing, while the photographs could bring home to mind.

dispositions.rationale: 中英文都补上了“按时登陆”这个前提，并写入登陆太晚时的备选：先越冬，在秋季和次年春季布置补给站，1915年尽早出发。英文另起一句转述备选部分，ev 增加 S-E23。

evidence.quote: Should this be done, the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once

Should the landing be made too late in the season, the party will go into winter quarters, lay out depots during the autumn and the following spring, and as early as possible in 1915 set out on the journey.

dispositions.rationale: 中英文都补出第二次尝试及其失败：行军七天，直线只前进七英里半，照此速度要三百多天才能到陆地，而食物只够四十二天，于是再次扎营，这才有了耐心营。ev 增加 S-E21。

evidence.quote: We had marched seven and a half miles in a direct line and at this rate it would take us over three hundred days to reach the land away to the west.
As we only had food for forty-two days there was no alternative, therefore, but to camp once more on the floe
Our new home, which we were to occupy for nearly three and a half months

dispositions.rationale: 删去“这一次他把等待写成了一个计划”这一前提。改为：行军前他已写下扎营等待外漂的方案，因确信应先尝试行军并考虑到心理层面而否决；海洋营是四天苦干后回到这个方案，再加上附近可能开出水道的指望。仍标为作者推断，ev 增加 S-E19。

evidence.quote: camp on the nearest heavy floe, scour the neighbouring pack for penguins and seals, and await the outward drift of the pack to open and navigable water.
Yet I feel sure that it is the right thing to attempt a march
There is a psychological aspect to the question also.

dispositions.rationale: 删去“没有说明原因”和“gives no reason”，改为转述他写下的理由：人在这种处境下需要占住思绪的东西和怀念家乡亲人的实物。英文逐字引用原句，ev 增加 S-E20。

evidence.quote: A man under such conditions needs something to occupy his thoughts, some tangible memento of his home and people beyond the seas. So sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept.

dispositions.rationale: 删去“重量或个人偏好”的推测和“超出了他写下的内容”。改为依据 S-E20 写明他的标准：他舍不得两磅限额，但认为有些个人物品不可或缺，因为旅程可能漫长、还可能在荒岸越冬。保留作者解读的标注。

evidence.quote: I rather grudged the two pounds allowance per man, owing to my keen anxiety to keep weights at a minimum, but some personal belongings could fairly be regarded as indispensable.
there was a possibility of a winter in improvised quarters on an inhospitable coast at the other end

dispositions.rationale: 已根据补入的摘录逐项修正：S-E23 对应 context.0（F1），S-E21 对应 story.13（F2），S-E19 对应 analysis.0（F3），S-E20 对应 analysis.2（F4、F5）。S-E22 与现稿没有矛盾，属于可选补充，未改动 hook 和 context。

evidence.quote: I propose to try to march with equipment across the ice in the direction of Paulet Island
